## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [previous review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13008#issuecomment-5804413559) and the [author reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13008#issuecomment-5808319283), checked at `f1c6c5d5`. The hover-suppression finding is resolved, and no regression was found in the changed code. The earlier Impact statement for touch input is corrected below.

**Verified:**

| Earlier claim (at `c8fc9ba4`) | At `f1c6c5d5` |
| --- | --- |
| Unpinning without hover leaves hover suppressed | Resolved: `TrayModel.toggleExpandedState` suppresses hover on unpin only when `drawerAreaHovered` is true. In the traced sequence (tap to pin, tap to unpin, mouse enters), the first hover now reveals the drawer |
| Test assertions ran against a copy of the drawer logic | Mostly resolved: the test now calls the production `TrayModel.js` helpers. Removing a hover-exit reset or a left-click call in `Tray.qml` now fails the suite, and so does dropping the menu flags inside `drawerRevealProgress` |
| Pin, hover-exit and open-menu behavior in both layouts | Still holds: no layout-specific lines changed, and unpinning while hovered still collapses the drawer immediately |

The helpers are pure functions that receive the QML properties as arguments, so the bindings still depend on the same properties as before.

### Correction: touch-tap impact

The previous review assumed that a touch tap reaches `toggleExpanded()` while `drawerAreaHovered` is false, and noted that Qt event ordering was untested. Qt 6.11 source (`QQuickDeliveryAgent`, `QQuickHoverHandler`) shows a different order:

```text
finger press    drawer HoverHandler -> hovered = true
finger release  chevron MouseArea clicked -> toggleExpanded()   (hovered still true)
                drawer HoverHandler sees the finger release -> hovered = false, suppression cleared
```

On this reading, an ordinary stationary tap unpins while hovered. That tap would not have left hover suppressed at `c8fc9ba4` either, so the earlier Impact ("the first mouse hover does not reveal it") overstated the touch case. The new conditional is still correct for any path that toggles without hover. This ordering comes from source reading only. It was not observed in a QML runtime or on touch hardware.

**Optional test improvement:** The structural checks match only the `TrayModel.<fn>(` prefixes and statement counts. In a sandboxed run, each of these single `Tray.qml` edits still passed all 43 assertions:
- `drawerHoverSuppressed = !next.drawerPinned`, which puts the earlier bug back on the QML side.
- Passing `false, false` as the menu flags to `drawerRevealProgress`.

Asserting the full assignment `drawerHoverSuppressed = next.drawerHoverSuppressed` and the full argument lists would catch both edits.

---

**Test scope:** Source inspection of the new commit, the shared bar and popup components, and qtdeclarative 6.11 pointer-delivery source. `test/shell.d/tray-test.sh` and single-edit variants of `Tray.qml` and `TrayModel.js` ran in an isolated sandbox under Deno's Node compatibility layer, not Node.js. There were no QML runtime, visual, pointer-timing, animation, popup or touch-hardware tests.
